rows.asked: what does the corpus mean by `keystone`, and how many documents are one
rows.why: the standard fixes four tiers and names the presumptive membership of each; `keystone` is its `Tier K`, defined by a machine-checked terminal at a pin

rows.asked: do the three tests measure one thing or two -- ROLE and APPARATUS
rows.why: the standard states the two properties as separate TIERS; it does not state that a single test can cross them, and the crossing is a measurement the standard does not contain

rows.asked: do the documents the apparatus axis marked deficient really lack what the taxonomy requires
rows.why: the taxonomy states the obligation the act measured against -- `grade . terminal . pin` -- and the act re-derived which element was missing

rows.asked: are the identifiers no kernel declares really absent
rows.why: a fact about kernels at refs, which no standard states or could state
the union already names the fourteen graded correspondence tables; the act re-measured a population the corpus had already listed

rows.asked: can role be read from what a document DRAWS ON
rows.why: a negative result about a method, and the standard proposes no method for reading role

rows.asked: does a control rebuilt to fail separate under co-location
rows.why: a second negative result about a second method, on a control the standard does not have

rows.asked: what does the evidence support about method
rows.why: the conclusion that a class ruling must rest on declaration -- which the standard already assumes in practice but nowhere argues
